title: Failover Clustering and Hyper-V HA in Plain English
summary: Understand how a Hyper-V failover cluster keeps VM roles available when a host is drained, maintained or fails.
plain_language_explanation: Failover Clustering coordinates multiple Windows Server nodes so clustered roles can move when a node is maintained or fails. For Hyper-V, the VM must be configured as a clustered role and the surrounding compute, network, storage and quorum design must all be healthy; clustering is not a substitute for fixing a shared dependency.
quick_check: Why can a VM be highly available at the host layer but still have an application outage?

title: Hyper-V Failover Cluster Architecture, Quorum and VM Role Availability
summary: Design and operate clustered Hyper-V with explicit failure domains, quorum awareness, validation and controlled role movement.
objective: Explain the availability contract of a Hyper-V failover cluster and distinguish planned role movement, node failure, quorum loss and shared-dependency failure.
body_outline: Cluster validation is evidence for supported and reliable design; hardware, networking, storage and system configuration must be validated before production reliance.
Quorum determines whether the cluster can continue making authoritative membership decisions; witness design should reflect node count, sites and failure domains.
A clustered Hyper-V VM role can restart or move between eligible nodes, but guest/application HA and external dependencies remain separate design concerns.
Node drain, maintenance and failover should preserve workload placement constraints and sufficient spare capacity rather than assuming every surviving node can absorb every VM.
quick_check: What evidence proves a cluster can survive the loss of its largest node without resource exhaustion?

title: Cluster Shared Volumes, Live Migration and Maintenance Mobility
summary: Operate CSV-backed Hyper-V workloads and live migration with explicit storage, network, authentication and bandwidth controls.
objective: Relate CSV access, coordinator behavior, live-migration paths and bandwidth governance to resilient maintenance and troubleshooting.
body_outline: CSV allows multiple cluster nodes concurrent access to a shared NTFS or ReFS volume so clustered workloads can move without remounting storage.
CSV redirected I/O is a diagnostic state with performance and path implications; investigate why it occurred rather than treating it as a harmless steady state.
Live migration moves a running VM between compatible hosts with minimal perceived downtime, but authentication, processor compatibility, storage access and network capacity remain prerequisites.
On Windows Server 2025 domain-joined servers, Credential Guard affects CredSSP-based live migration; Kerberos constrained delegation is the safer planned model where applicable.
When SMB is used for live migration, bandwidth governance prevents migration traffic from starving storage or cluster communications.
quick_check: Why should a successful live migration test include workload latency and cluster-network observations rather than only the final VM owner node?

title: Cluster-Aware Updating, Drain Strategy and Failure-Domain Maintenance
summary: Design patching and host maintenance so clustered Hyper-V workloads retain capacity, placement correctness and recoverability throughout the maintenance window.
architecture_notes: Cluster-Aware Updating orchestrates node maintenance sequentially: place a node in maintenance, move clustered roles, apply updates, restart if required, restore the node and continue. Availability still depends on pre-update cluster health, quorum, workload mobility, capacity and consistent update sources.
failure_modes: starting maintenance with validation or cluster-health faults
insufficient spare capacity after draining a node
VM anti-affinity or placement constraints ignored
CSV or live-migration degradation hidden before patching
automatic update policy competing with CAU
failed node reintroduced without post-update health verification
enterprise_design_notes: Treat maintenance as a controlled availability exercise: define N+1 capacity, verify quorum and witness, preview CAU readiness, preserve change evidence, drain one failure domain at a time, validate workloads after each node, and stop the run when health deviates from the acceptance criteria.

title: Read-Only Hyper-V Cluster, CSV and Mobility Readiness Evidence Pack
summary: Collect cluster, node, VM-role, CSV and migration evidence without moving workloads or changing cluster state.
objective: Produce a timestamped readiness pack before maintenance, failover testing or live migration is approved.
steps: Record cluster name, functional state, quorum resource and node membership.
Record node state and current ownership distribution of clustered roles.
List clustered VM roles and correlate them with Hyper-V VM state and owner node.
Record CSV name, owner/coordinator, state and path; flag redirected or degraded conditions for investigation.
Record cluster networks and live-migration configuration without initiating movement.
Capture recent failover-clustering warnings/errors and document unresolved blockers before approving maintenance.
expected_result: A read-only cluster readiness pack with no role moves, node pauses, CSV state changes or migrations.

title: Clustered Hyper-V Failover, CSV or Live Migration Incident Decision Tree
summary: Diagnose clustered VM movement and storage-path failures without turning a transient symptom into a second outage.
diagnostic_order: Define whether the incident is VM-role failover, live migration, CSV/storage access, cluster membership or guest/application availability.
Confirm cluster/node/group state and quorum before attempting movement.
Check CSV state, coordinator/owner and storage-path evidence; identify redirected or unavailable access.
Check source/destination host compatibility, authentication and live-migration network reachability.
Correlate FailoverClustering, Hyper-V-VMMS and storage/network events by timestamp.
Compare the failing VM or node with a healthy peer and preserve evidence before remediation.
escalation_boundary: Do not force quorum, clear cluster configuration, evict nodes, change witness/quorum, move CSV ownership, alter cluster networks, disable security controls or repeatedly force-migrate production VMs during diagnosis without approved recovery/change authority.

title: Hyper-V Cluster HA and Maintenance Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment covering quorum, CSV, live migration, maintenance capacity and Cluster-Aware Updating.

assessment_items.question: Why must quorum be checked before taking another cluster node down for maintenance?
assessment_items.answer: Because losing enough voting participation can cause the cluster to stop rather than risk split-brain membership decisions.

assessment_items.question: A CSV enters redirected mode. What is the correct first response?
assessment_items.answer: Preserve cluster and storage-path evidence, determine why direct I/O is unavailable, assess workload impact and fix the underlying path or maintenance condition rather than blindly moving ownership.

assessment_items.question: Why can a live migration succeed technically but still be operationally unacceptable?
assessment_items.answer: Migration can consume CPU or network bandwidth, expose latency, violate placement expectations or leave insufficient failover capacity even though the VM reaches the destination.

assessment_items.question: What must be true before a CAU run is treated as low risk?
assessment_items.answer: Cluster validation/health, quorum, update source consistency, workload mobility, spare capacity, maintenance policy and stop/rollback criteria must all be verified.

title: Senior Hyper-V Interview: Cluster HA, CSV and Maintenance Operations
summary: Senior production scenarios testing failover reasoning, quorum safety, CSV diagnosis, migration governance and patching design.

questions.question: You must patch a five-node Hyper-V cluster hosting 420 VMs. What is your go/no-go sequence before draining node one?
answer_points: verify cluster validation and unresolved alerts
verify quorum/witness and failure domains
prove N+1 compute and storage capacity
verify CSV health and live-migration paths
review placement/anti-affinity and critical workloads
preview update readiness and consistent update source
define stop criteria and post-node validation

questions.question: A CSV is online but several VMs show storage latency. How do you separate CSV coordination from physical storage failure?
answer_points: record CSV state/coordinator and redirected access
correlate storage-path and cluster events
compare affected and healthy CSVs/nodes
inspect network path if redirected I/O is active
validate underlying array/MPIO/SMB evidence as applicable
avoid ownership moves until the failure domain is understood

questions.question: Live migration fails after upgrading hosts to Windows Server 2025. What security change belongs high on the hypothesis list?
answer_points: Credential Guard is enabled by default on eligible domain-joined Windows Server 2025 systems
CredSSP-based delegation can therefore fail
verify configured authentication rather than disabling Credential Guard
use supported Kerberos constrained delegation where applicable
still validate DNS/SPNs/network/CPU/storage prerequisites

questions.question: Why is repeated forced failover a poor troubleshooting strategy?
answer_points: it destroys temporal evidence
can amplify storage/network faults
may exhaust remaining capacity
can trigger guest/application recovery repeatedly
can obscure quorum or placement problems
diagnose the failure domain before controlled remediation
